title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: The written factor looks like 'k' ('multiplication par k', 'si k inv.') while the degree is called n. It should read multiplication by n; this is a notational slip, not a mathematical error.

Transposition of d and δ holds only up to sign and normalisation conventions, which are not checked on the page. The required normalisation of the pairings Sym×Γ and Λ×Λ is also not specified. This is harmless but unverified.

The pairing statements are made 'degree by degree'. Perfectness needs M projective of finite type in each degree, which is stated; for general M the induced map to the dual is not an isomorphism, which is implicitly acknowledged.

ideas.what: In char 0, H^0_DR(Sym*M) = A because δ∘d = n on Sym^nM, so d is injective in positive degree. More generally this holds if n is invertible, and M is arbitrary (no flatness).
ideas.modern_name: Algebraic Poincaré lemma for polynomial algebras via the Euler operator (homotopy dδ+δd = degree)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical; folklore. In Koszul/de Rham functorial form it appears in e.g. Illusie (Complexe cotangent), and Franjou–Friedlander–Scorichenko–Suslin 1999

ideas.what: Pairing M⊗M'→A induces perfect dualities Sym^n M × Γ^n M' → A and Λ^q M × Λ^q M' → A for M projective of finite type.
ideas.modern_name: Duality between symmetric and divided powers (Γ^n(M^∨) ≅ (Sym^n M)^∨)

ideas.what: The de Rham complex of Sym*M is the transpose of the Koszul complex of Γ*M^∨, and the Koszul complex of Sym*M is the transpose of the divided-power de Rham complex of Γ*M^∨. Multiplication is dual to comultiplication.
ideas.modern_name: Duality (Kuhn/Koszul-type duality) between de Rham and Koszul complexes Sym⊗Λ and Γ⊗Λ
ideas.usually_credited_to: Used systematically in functor cohomology: Franjou–Friedlander–Scorichenko–Suslin (1999), Totaro (1997); also implicit in Berthelot–Ogus / Illusie on divided-power de Rham complexes

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up, around 1976, the full system of four complexes (de Rham and Koszul on Sym and on Γ) together with their transposition duality. This is the exact framework later used as a basic tool in strict polynomial functor cohomology (FFSS, Totaro). It is a historical precursor rather than a new result.
missed.quote: on vérifie que les op. d_M et δ_{M'}, δ_M et d_{M'} sont en transposition par cet accouplement
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical credit only. It documents that the de Rham/Koszul duality on Sym⊗Λ and Γ⊗Λ was part of Grothendieck's unpublished 1976 IHÉS lecture material on the divided-power de Rham complex.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is standard: the Euler-operator Poincaré lemma and the duality of Sym and Γ transposing de Rham and Koszul differentials. It is carefully done, without flatness, and is a mild precursor of later functor-cohomology tools, but nothing a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: 'on trouve la multiplication par k' and 'ça marche si k inv. dans A': the letter is plausibly k in the manuscript but denotes the degree n.
'Donc dans le cas de ce dualité parfaite' should read 'Donc dans le cas de cette dualité parfaite'.
'S^*Λ^*(M) × Γ^*Λ^*(M')' means (S^*⊗Λ^*)(M) × (Γ^*⊗Λ^*)(M'); the struck-out word before it is 'Sym'.
The inserted note '{+M≃Sym^1 M+}' is written under the arrow δ (as 'Sym^1 M' under '⊗M'), i.e. identifying M with Sym^1 M.
